title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who led the army to waste the country of the children of Ammon?
questions.correctAnswer: Joab
questions.explanation: Joab led forth the power of the army against the children of Ammon as stated in 1 Chronicles 20:1.

questions.question: Where did David remain while Joab besieged Rabbah?
questions.correctAnswer: At Jerusalem
questions.explanation: David tarried at Jerusalem while Joab besieged Rabbah according to 1 Chronicles 20:1.

questions.question: What did David take from the king of the children of Ammon after the city was captured?
questions.correctAnswer: A crown
questions.explanation: David took the crown of their king from off his head as recorded in 1 Chronicles 20:2.

questions.question: How much did the crown David took weigh?
questions.correctAnswer: A talent of gold
questions.explanation: The crown was found to weigh a talent of gold as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 20:2.

questions.question: What did David do with the people he brought out of the city of Rabbah?
options: Cut them with saws and harrows of iron and axes
questions.correctAnswer: Cut them with saws and harrows of iron and axes
questions.explanation: David cut the people with saws, harrows of iron, and axes as described in 1 Chronicles 20:3.

questions.question: True or False: Joab destroyed the city of Rabbah after besieging it.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joab smote Rabbah and destroyed it as stated in 1 Chronicles 20:1.

questions.question: True or False: David personally led the army to besiege Rabbah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joab led the army, while David stayed in Jerusalem according to 1 Chronicles 20:1.

questions.question: What was set upon David's head from the king of the children of Ammon?
questions.correctAnswer: A crown
questions.explanation: The crown taken from the king was set upon David's head as noted in 1 Chronicles 20:2.

questions.question: What kind of spoil did David bring out of the city?
questions.correctAnswer: Exceeding much
questions.explanation: David brought out exceeding much spoil from the city as stated in 1 Chronicles 20:2.

questions.question: After dealing with Rabbah, where did David and all the people return to?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: David and all the people returned to Jerusalem as recorded in 1 Chronicles 20:3.

questions.question: What tools were used to cut the people brought out of Rabbah?
options: Saws, harrows of iron, and axes
questions.correctAnswer: Saws, harrows of iron, and axes
questions.explanation: The text specifies saws, harrows of iron, and axes as the tools used according to 1 Chronicles 20:3.

questions.question: Which of these events happened first in 1 Chronicles 20?
options: David took the crown from the king
David and people returned to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Joab besieged Rabbah
questions.explanation: The siege by Joab happened first, followed by smiting Rabbah, David taking the crown, and finally returning to Jerusalem as per 1 Chronicles 20:1-3.

questions.question: True or False: David dealt with all the cities of the children of Ammon in the same way he did with Rabbah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David dealt so with all the cities of the children of Ammon as stated in 1 Chronicles 20:3.

questions.question: True or False: The crown taken from the king contained precious stones.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The crown was adorned with precious stones according to 1 Chronicles 20:2.

questions.question: Who is credited with smiting and destroying Rabbah?
questions.correctAnswer: Joab
questions.explanation: Joab smote and destroyed Rabbah as described in 1 Chronicles 20:1.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who slew Sippai, the son of the giant, during the war at Gezer with the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: Sibbechai the Hushathite
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:4 states that Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Sippai, who was of the children of the giant, during the war at Gezer with the Philistines.

questions.question: What is the significance of Elhanan slaying Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, in the context of faith and courage?
options: It shows that faith in God enables believers to overcome great foes
It demonstrates that only kings can defeat giants
It means that weapons are more important than faith
It shows that Goliath's family was invincible
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that faith in God enables believers to overcome great foes
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:5 records Elhanan slaying Lahmi, brother of Goliath, emphasizing that God empowers His people to face and overcome intimidating enemies, as also seen in 1 Chronicles 20:4 and 20:7.

questions.question: How does the account of the man with 24 fingers and toes in Gath teach about humility and reliance on God?
options: Physical stature does not guarantee victory over God’s people
More fingers and toes mean greater strength
God favors those with physical might
questions.correctAnswer: Physical stature does not guarantee victory over God’s people
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:6 describes a giant with extraordinary physical features who was defeated, showing that God's power, not physical size, determines victory, as reinforced in 1 Chronicles 20:7 where Jonathan kills him.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 20:7 teach us about the role of family support in spiritual battles?
options: Jonathan, David’s brother, played a crucial role by slaying the giant who defied Israel
Only kings can fight for Israel
Family relations are irrelevant in spiritual struggles
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan, David’s brother, played a crucial role by slaying the giant who defied Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:7 shows Jonathan, David's brother, actively defending Israel by killing the giant, illustrating the importance of family unity and support in spiritual and physical battles, in connection with verses 6 and 8.

questions.question: Based on 1 Chronicles 20:4-5, what can we learn about God’s providence in times of repeated conflict?
options: God empowers His servants repeatedly to overcome enemies
Conflict is always caused by human failure
God allows giants to dominate Israel
Victory depends solely on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers His servants repeatedly to overcome enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 show multiple wars against the Philistines where God used different men to defeat enemies, teaching that God’s providence sustains His people through repeated challenges.

questions.question: True or False: The man slain by Jonathan had exactly 20 fingers and toes.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:6 clearly states the man had 24 fingers and toes, six on each hand and foot, not 20.

questions.question: What practical lesson about courage can a believer draw from Elhanan's victory over Lahmi according to 1 Chronicles 20:5?
options: Courage supported by faith helps believers face seemingly impossible odds
Only warriors can serve God effectively
questions.correctAnswer: Courage supported by faith helps believers face seemingly impossible odds
questions.explanation: Elhanan’s defeat of Lahmi, a giant, in 1 Chronicles 20:5 teaches that courage rooted in faith allows believers to overcome formidable challenges, as supported by the accounts in verses 4 and 7.

questions.question: How does the repeated mention of wars in 1 Chronicles 20:4-6 emphasize the necessity of perseverance in faith?
options: God’s people must remain faithful and persevere through multiple trials
Wars show that belief is not important
Only one victory is necessary for faith
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people must remain faithful and persevere through multiple trials
questions.explanation: The multiple conflicts in verses 4 to 6 illustrate ongoing challenges where perseverance and faith are essential, teaching believers to trust God continually.

questions.question: True or False: The giant defeated by Jonathan was the only giant mentioned in 1 Chronicles 20.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20 mentions several giants: Sippai in verse 4, Lahmi in verse 5, and the tall man with 24 fingers and toes in verse 6, indicating multiple giants were involved.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 20:8 imply about the legacy of giants in Gath and God’s sovereignty?
options: All giants born in Gath were defeated by David and his servants
Giants were invincible and ruled Israel
God allowed giants to dominate forever
Giants formed an alliance with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: All giants born in Gath were defeated by David and his servants
questions.explanation: Verse 8 summarizes that the giants born in Gath fell by the hand of David and his servants, showing God’s sovereign power over even the mightiest opponents.

questions.question: How does the defeat of multiple giants in 1 Chronicles 20 encourage believers facing overwhelming challenges?
options: Trusting God enables victory over seemingly unbeatable foes
Fighting giants is impossible for believers
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God enables victory over seemingly unbeatable foes
questions.explanation: The repeated victories over giants (verses 4-8) encourage believers to rely on God’s power rather than physical might in overcoming challenges.

questions.question: What does the story of Joab besieging Rabbah in 1 Chronicles 20:1-3 teach about obedience and leadership?
options: Obedience to God’s timing and leadership brings success
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s timing and leadership brings success
questions.explanation: Joab led the army and took Rabbah while David stayed in Jerusalem (verse 1), showing that following God’s timing and respecting roles leads to victory, connected to the faithfulness shown in the middle verses.

questions.question: Based on 1 Chronicles 20:4-5, what role do individual acts of courage play in the community’s victory?
options: Individual acts of courage contribute decisively to the community’s overall success
questions.correctAnswer: Individual acts of courage contribute decisively to the community’s overall success
questions.explanation: Sibbechai and Elhanan’s courageous acts in verses 4 and 5 were crucial in subduing enemies, illustrating how personal faith and bravery can impact the whole community.

questions.question: A believer struggles with fear when facing difficult situations. Based on 1 Chronicles 20, which biblical truth applies?
options: God empowers His people to overcome giants and fears through faith and courage
Fear is a sign of weak faith and must be ignored
Physical strength alone will conquer all problems
Avoid all conflict to be safe
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers His people to overcome giants and fears through faith and courage
questions.explanation: The repeated victories over giants by God’s servants in verses 4-7 teach that God strengthens believers to face and overcome their fears and challenges.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 20:2, David personally led the siege of Rabbah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:1 states Joab led the army and besieged Rabbah while David stayed in Jerusalem; he did not personally lead the siege.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who was the person that slew the giant at Gath with six fingers and six toes on each hand and foot?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan the son of Shimea
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:7 states that Jonathan the son of Shimea, David's brother, slew the giant who defied Israel at Gath.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 20, how many fingers and toes did the giant at Gath have?
options: Twenty-four total, six on each hand and foot
Twenty total, five on each hand and foot
Thirty total, seven on each hand and foot
Eighteen total, four on each hand and foot
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-four total, six on each hand and foot
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:6 describes a giant with twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and six on each foot.

questions.question: What weapon characteristic is mentioned about Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite?
options: His spear staff was like a weaver's beam
His sword was as long as a vineyard
His shield was made of bronze
His bow could shoot three arrows at once
questions.correctAnswer: His spear staff was like a weaver's beam
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:5 states that Lahmi's spear staff was like a weaver's beam, indicating its great size and weight.

questions.question: What is the significance of the crown taken by David from the king of the children of Ammon?
options: It weighed a talent of gold and had precious stones
It was made of pure silver
It was cursed and brought misfortune
It was inscribed with the name of David
questions.correctAnswer: It weighed a talent of gold and had precious stones
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:2 records that David took the crown from the Ammonite king’s head; it weighed a talent of gold and was adorned with precious stones.

questions.question: Which city did Joab besiege and destroy while David stayed in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Rabbah
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:1 tells us that Joab led the army and besieged Rabbah, ultimately smiting and destroying it while David tarried in Jerusalem.

questions.question: The wars mentioned in this chapter against giants and Philistines highlight the ongoing conflict between Israel and which peoples?
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines and Ammonites
questions.explanation: Throughout 1 Chronicles 20, the conflicts involve the Philistines (giants) and the Ammonites, as seen in verses 1-8.

questions.question: What cruel method did David use on the people taken from the city of Rabbah?
options: Cut them with saws, harrows of iron, and axes
questions.correctAnswer: Cut them with saws, harrows of iron, and axes
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:3 specifies that David brought out the people and cut them with saws, harrows of iron, and axes.

questions.question: Which of the following battles described in this chapter is associated with the city Gezer?
options: Jonathan slew the giant at Gath
questions.correctAnswer: Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Sippai
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:4 states that war arose at Gezer where Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Sippai, a giant.

questions.question: True or False: The giants mentioned in 1 Chronicles 20 were all killed by David himself.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:8 clarifies that the giants fell by the hand of David and his servants, indicating others besides David killed some giants.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'a talent of gold' used in 1 Chronicles 20:2 refers to a significant weight and value of gold.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:2 mentions the crown weighed a talent of gold, a large ancient unit of weight indicating great value.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage recounts David's defeat of Goliath, a theme echoed in 1 Chronicles 20 with the killing of giants?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 17
questions.explanation: The killing of giants in 1 Chronicles 20 echoes the narrative of David defeating Goliath in 1 Samuel 17, exemplifying God's deliverance through David.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the listing of multiple battles against giants in 1 Chronicles 20 to emphasize Israel's victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter begins and ends with battles against giants, framing the section and using inclusio to emphasize Israel's conquest (see 1 Chronicles 20:1 and 20:8).

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'giant' used in 1 Chronicles 20 is 'Rephaim'. What is the significance of this term in ancient Near Eastern context?
options: It refers to legendary ancient warriors or spirits of the dead
It is a term for foreign kings
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to legendary ancient warriors or spirits of the dead
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Rephaim' often refers to giants or mighty warriors and in some contexts to shades or spirits of the dead in the ancient Near East (see 1 Chronicles 20:4).

questions.question: How does the defeat of the giants in 1 Chronicles 20 symbolically foreshadow New Testament themes of Christ's victory over evil?
options: David’s triumph over giants prefigures Christ’s victory over Satan and sin
It symbolizes the coming of a new temple
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem
It foreshadows the exile to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: David’s triumph over giants prefigures Christ’s victory over Satan and sin
questions.explanation: The giants represent formidable enemies; David’s victory foreshadows Christ’s ultimate defeat of spiritual evil as seen in the New Testament (cf. Hebrews 2:14).

questions.question: Which of David’s family members is mentioned as the killer of the giant in Gath in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan, son of Shimea
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:7 identifies Jonathan, son of Shimea (David's brother), as the one who slew the giant who defied Israel.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 20:1 demonstrate about God's providence in the context of warfare during King David's reign?
options: God directs the timing and outcome of battles through His appointed leaders.
God is indifferent to the affairs of kings and battles.
Victory in battle depends solely on human strength and strategy.
The king must personally lead all battles to receive God's blessing.
questions.correctAnswer: God directs the timing and outcome of battles through His appointed leaders.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:1 shows that Joab led the army and successfully besieged Rabbah while David stayed in Jerusalem, indicating divine orchestration over leadership and victory in battle. This aligns with Proverbs 21:31 where victory is from the LORD.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 20:2, what theological significance can be seen in David placing the Ammonite king's crown on his own head?
options: It symbolizes God's sovereign authority over all earthly kings.
It was a sign of David's pride and ambition.
It was a ritual to invoke the gods of Ammon.
It shows David's desire to become an Ammonite king.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's sovereign authority over all earthly kings.
questions.explanation: David placing the crown, which weighed a talent of gold and contained precious stones, on his head symbolizes the transfer of authority under God's sovereign will, demonstrating God's supremacy over nations and their rulers (1 Chronicles 20:2).

questions.question: What doctrine of divine justice is reflected in David's treatment of the Ammonite people as described in 1 Chronicles 20:3?
options: God enacts retributive justice against nations opposing His people.
God commands mercy and forgiveness without exception.
Human justice is separate from divine judgment.
War is a human invention without divine sanction.
questions.correctAnswer: God enacts retributive justice against nations opposing His people.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 20:3 describes severe judgment on the Ammonites, reflecting the doctrine that God executes retributive justice against those who oppose His covenant people, consistent with Old Testament theodicy (Deuteronomy 32:35).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly illustrated by Sibbechai’s victory over Sippai in 1 Chronicles 20:4?
options: God's omnipotence in empowering His servants to overcome giants.
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence in empowering His servants to overcome giants.
questions.explanation: Sibbechai’s slaying of a giant (Sippai) during war illustrates God's omnipotence, as He empowers His people to triumph over seemingly insurmountable foes (1 Chronicles 20:4), reminiscent of 2 Samuel 21:15-17.

questions.question: What theological insight about Christ as the ultimate victor over sin and death can be drawn from Elhanan's victory over Lahmi, Goliath's brother, in 1 Chronicles 20:5?
options: God raises up instruments to defeat the 'giant' powers opposing His kingdom, foreshadowing Christ’s victory over evil.
Only David can defeat the enemies of Israel.
Giants represent insurmountable physical foes only.
Victory in battle is unrelated to spiritual victory.
questions.correctAnswer: God raises up instruments to defeat the 'giant' powers opposing His kingdom, foreshadowing Christ’s victory over evil.
questions.explanation: Elhanan’s victory over Lahmi, brother of Goliath, symbolizes God’s provision of victors over formidable enemies, prefiguring Christ’s ultimate triumph over Satan and sin (1 Chronicles 20:5; Colossians 2:15).

questions.question: How does the description of the giant in Gath in 1 Chronicles 20:6 contribute to biblical anthropology?
options: It highlights the existence of extraordinary beings in opposition to God’s people, emphasizing human vulnerability and the need for divine intervention.
It teaches that giants were the original rulers of the earth.
It suggests human beings were created with extra fingers and toes.
It denies the reality of supernatural evil.
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the existence of extraordinary beings in opposition to God’s people, emphasizing human vulnerability and the need for divine intervention.
questions.explanation: The giant’s unusual physical traits in 1 Chronicles 20:6 emphasize the extraordinary threats faced by Israel, underscoring human frailty and the necessity of God's deliverance (Psalm 44:3).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s providence and human agency is taught by Jonathan’s slaying of the giant in 1 Chronicles 20:7?
options: God providentially uses human agents to accomplish His purposes.
God directly intervenes without human involvement.
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially uses human agents to accomplish His purposes.
questions.explanation: Jonathan, David’s brother, kills the giant (1 Chronicles 20:7), demonstrating that God sovereignly works through human agency to fulfill His plans (Acts 17:26).

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 20:8, what theological conclusion is suggested by the repeated defeat of giants by David and his servants?
options: God ensures the triumph of His covenant people over spiritual and physical enemies.
Giants were invincible and defeated Israel.
Victory was due to human superiority only.
David’s servants acted independently of God.
questions.correctAnswer: God ensures the triumph of His covenant people over spiritual and physical enemies.
questions.explanation: The verse shows that all giants born in Gath fell by David and his servants’ hands, indicating God’s faithfulness to protect and advance His people against enemies (1 Chronicles 20:8; Psalm 44:5).

questions.question: What combined theological teaching about divine justice and human responsibility emerges when considering 1 Chronicles 20:3 and 1 Chronicles 20:8 together?
options: God enacts justice through His people, who are responsible to execute His will against evil.
God acts alone without involving humans in judgment.
Justice is arbitrary and unrelated to covenant faithfulness.
Humans must seek justice apart from God’s direction.
questions.correctAnswer: God enacts justice through His people, who are responsible to execute His will against evil.
questions.explanation: Both verses show David and his servants carrying out God’s judgment on enemies, demonstrating the doctrine that God’s justice is realized through human agents acting under divine authority (1 Chronicles 20:3,8; Romans 13:4).

questions.question: How do 1 Chronicles 20:4 and 1 Chronicles 20:7 together illustrate the doctrine of spiritual warfare in the life of God's people?
options: God empowers His servants to confront and overcome spiritual and physical manifestations of evil.
Spiritual warfare is irrelevant to physical battles.
Victory comes through human strength alone.
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers His servants to confront and overcome spiritual and physical manifestations of evil.
questions.explanation: The defeats of giants by Sibbechai (v.4) and Jonathan (v.7) symbolize God’s empowerment in spiritual warfare, showing His people triumph over evil forces through divine strength (Ephesians 6:12; 1 Chronicles 20:4,7).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the brutal treatment of captured peoples in 1 Chronicles 20:3 reflects an immoral God. What does this passage actually teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: The passage reveals God's righteous judgment against sin and His holiness demanding justice.
God is indifferent to human suffering.
The passage is purely historical without moral significance.
questions.correctAnswer: The passage reveals God's righteous judgment against sin and His holiness demanding justice.
questions.explanation: David’s harsh actions reflect the execution of divine justice against persistent enemies (1 Chronicles 20:3), illustrating God's holy wrath against sin and His requirement for justice (Isaiah 5:16).

questions.question: What attribute of God is most evident in 1 Chronicles 20:2 through the description of the crown’s weight and precious stones?
options: God’s majesty and glory as King over all nations.
God’s transcendence only, without involvement in history.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s majesty and glory as King over all nations.
questions.explanation: The crown’s rich description symbolizes God’s majestic kingship over the nations, showing His glory and sovereign rule (1 Chronicles 20:2; Psalm 47:2).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 20:5 contribute to our understanding of Christological typology within the Davidic narrative?
options: It typifies Christ as the victor over the spiritual enemies of God's kingdom.
It denies any connection between David’s servants and Christ.
It focuses only on human military history.
It suggests Christ’s victory is unrelated to Israel’s history.
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies Christ as the victor over the spiritual enemies of God's kingdom.
questions.explanation: Elhanan’s defeat of Lahmi, brother of Goliath, is a type pointing to Christ’s ultimate victory over evil forces, fulfilling the Davidic promise of a Messiah (1 Chronicles 20:5; Hebrews 2:14).

questions.question: What does the repeated theme of ‘giants’ being defeated in 1 Chronicles 20:4–8 teach about the nature of salvation history?
options: God’s people are continually delivered from formidable evil by His power, foreshadowing ultimate redemption.
Giants represent physical rather than spiritual struggles only.
Salvation history lacks conflict or opposition.
Victory is purely symbolic with no historical basis.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people are continually delivered from formidable evil by His power, foreshadowing ultimate redemption.
questions.explanation: The defeats of giants symbolize God’s ongoing deliverance of His covenant people from evil, pointing forward to the full salvation through Christ (1 Chronicles 20:4–8; Revelation 12:7-9).

questions.question: What combined theological understanding about divine sovereignty and human obedience can be drawn from 1 Chronicles 20:1 and 1 Chronicles 20:7?
options: God sovereignly directs history and calls His people to faithful obedience in carrying out His purposes.
Human obedience guarantees success without God’s involvement.
Victory is accidental and unrelated to faithfulness.
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs history and calls His people to faithful obedience in carrying out His purposes.
questions.explanation: Joab leading the army (v.1) and Jonathan killing the giant (v.7) show God’s sovereign guidance and the necessity of human obedience to His will (1 Chronicles 20:1,7; Joshua 1:7).
